sre-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-pool-saturation eu-dedicated-1 - queue_depth=162, p95=1.2s -> 3.8s, p99=4.9s -> 9.1s, streaming stalls spike. Autoscaler handshake failures observed. Paging oncall: Maya H @here

Maya H: I'm oncall, responding. Seeing clear tail blowup on eu-dedicated-1 starting ~10:42 UTC. p95 jumped from ~1.2s to ~3.8s, p99 up to ~9s. Streaming sessions showing repeated "chunk_timeout" errors. Going to pull autoscaler and pool logs.

Tom K: I can join. Autoscaler traces show a bunch of warmup registrations timing out. Looks like new nodes register but never report "ready" before handshake TTL. Example from autoscaler log:
```
2026-03-15T10:42:33Z autoscaler: warmup_register(pool=eu-dedicated-1, node=n-49) -> timeout after 30s
2026-03-15T10:42:34Z runtime: kv-cache-miss spike for model rdx-large (seq=2048)
2026-03-15T10:42:35Z autoscaler: scale_up accepted -> provisioning (request_id=0x7bfc)
2026-03-15T10:42:58Z autoscaler: node n-49 failed healthcheck, deregister
```

Leah R: Looks like warmup is the choke. If nodes can't finish model init the pool stays at old capacity and queue backs up. Two immediate mitigations: 1) route heavy streaming requests to hosted hotshot pool for short window, 2) trigger manual scale (force additional warm nodes) and extend handshake TTL temporarily. We should also consider fallback to rdx-small-quant for new requests to reduce init time.

Maya H: I agree. I'm going to trigger manual scale now and open an incident channel. Also disabling streaming for routes that are timing out >30s to avoid long-held connections. Doing a manual scale call: 
```bash
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/provision/pools/eu-dedicated-1/scale" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"delta_replicas":4, "handshake_ttl":60}'
```

sre-bot: Action acknowledged: scale request submitted (req=0x7bfc-2). Telemetry: queue_depth -> 162 -> 140 within 30s.

Tom K: Confirming autoscaler control-plane shows nodes provisioning but runtime logs show repeated "OOM during init" for rdx-large on these GPUs — likely quantization/loader memory pressure during warmup. Suggest pinning new nodes to smaller model or skipping loading model weights until node healthchecks pass.

Leah R: I can patch routing for the next 10m to prefer hosted-hotshot for models flagged rdx-large with streaming=true. Patch command (internal): 
```
POST /routing/priority 
{ "match": {"model": "rdx-large", "streaming": true}, "target": "hosted-hotshot", "ttl": 600 }
```
Apply now?

Maya H: Apply it. Carl, can you coordinate CS status updates? We need to know which customers are hitting streaming failures.

Carl S: ACME and BetaFin flagged with 504s and aborted streams. I'm drafting an advisory blurb: "We're seeing increased latency and intermittent streaming failures for dedicated EU pools; routing & mitigation in progress; next update in 15m." Posting to status page and notifying account owners. :loudspeaker:

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: Dedicated Pool Saturation (internal) https://runbooks.redwood/incidents/dedicated-sat - steps: verify queue depth, trigger manual scale, enable fallback routing, contact infra lead.

Maya H: Manual scale resulted in 3 new nodes becoming ready around 10:45 UTC; queue depth down to ~98. However p99 still elevated and streaming stalls continue intermittently. Next step: enable model fallback for new requests to rdx-medium-quant and convert active streaming requests >30s to polling responses (disable chunked streaming) to reduce tail holding. Doing fallback toggle now.

Tom K: Watcher: also seeing KV-cache coldpath -> spike in token generation times. That will keep p99 high until caches warm. We can pre-warm caches for rdx-medium-quant on new nodes by issuing a synthetic warmup: 
```bash
for i in {1..10}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://internal-api/redwood/warmup -d '{"model":"rdx-medium-quant","prompt":"warmup"}' &\
done
```
I'll kick that after the fallback is live.

Maya H: Fallback enabled at 10:48 UTC. Routing change applied. Synthetic warmups started. Customer impact: Carl, any change?

Carl S: ACME reports partial improvement; fewer aborted streams but some degraded latency. BetaFin still seeing occasional 504s. I'm escalating to their TAM, and adding notes to the incident.

Leah R: Suggested post-incident action items: 1) increase handshake_ttl during burst windows, 2) add early model-init health probe to prevent nodes flapping, 3) create autoscaler mitigation mode that allows short-lived accepting without full model load for warm traffic, 4) investigate quant memory profile for rdx-large.

Maya H: Agreed. Opening incident (INC-2026-1873). Next update in 15m or on any major change. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
